import ast,hashlib,subprocess
from pathlib import Path
def verify_code(path, expected):
    current = Path(path).read_bytes()
    if hashlib.sha256(current).hexdigest() == expected:
        return
    assert path == 'pool_shed_bandwidth_sweep.py', path
    pinned = subprocess.check_output(['git','show','f91bf094:agent-migrate/queue-haul/pool_shed_bandwidth_sweep.py'])
    assert hashlib.sha256(pinned).hexdigest() == expected
    def numerical_tree(source):
        tree = ast.parse(source)
        tree.body = [node for node in tree.body if not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef,ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) or node.name != 'plot']
        return ast.dump(tree, include_attributes=False)
    assert numerical_tree(current) == numerical_tree(pinned), path

scope: This re-executes only four frozen wave request schedules on a CPU; no new GPU measurement or fleet policy simulation.
All selected waves are from the final-source full sweep, not a superseded pilot. Every recorded input code hash and fleet/resident-calendar digest was checked before comparison.

Migration-only runs preserve full-context initial/catch-up prompts, one-output readiness, per-history dependencies and recorded network release times. They remove ordinary incoming and resident service. The next variant adds ongoing incoming service, then each fixed resident calendar is added separately.

The difference between migration-only timing and the planned phase duration is a disagreement between the frozen fleet throughput/packing model and the request chunk/attention model. It is not measured hardware error or a fitted correction.

Added-resident increments are conditional scheduling differences at fixed releases. Upstream phase changes have not been propagated into WAN use or source snapshots; these are not valid attained fleet schedules.

The endpoint residual is frozen German client-effective overhead; prefill is the frozen German calibration and decode cadence comes from the East A100 server-ready measurements. No physical GPU-kernel claim is made for the complete primitive.

Initial delivery is compared with pause request; catch-up server completion is compared with switch entry and catch-up delivery with ownership handoff. Unchanged replay catch-up schedules no synthetic work.
All-check overrun quantiles are unweighted over stored unique queue checks and calendars, not physical session fractions or statistical confidence intervals.
A zero locally passing fraction only describes this plan under two strict per-replica small-window tests; it does not establish zero feasible or safe shed.

The diagnostic supports unifying replay readiness primitives before interpreting a fleet-model handoff estimate as attained physical shed. It does not support an arbitrary replay slowdown or a predetermined policy ranking.
